title: The Harmonic Series
description: A quick introduction to overtones and the ratios they create.

title.label: Title
title.heading: The Harmonic Series
title.body: The harmonic series is the ladder of overtones above a fundamental pitch. Each partial adds a whole-number multiple of the base frequency, which is why it is so useful for understanding consonance and tuning.

prerequisites.label: Just Intonation
prerequisites.body: Review how simple frequency ratios become intervals, triads, and tuning systems.

relatedConcepts.label: Subharmonic Series
relatedConcepts.body: Compare the harmonic ladder with its inverted counterpart and hear how the ratio family changes.

qa.label: Q&A
qa.question: Why does the harmonic series matter in xenharmonic music?

choices.text: It shows how many unrelated pitches fit inside one octave.
It reveals simple frequency ratios that inspire intervals, chords, and tunings.
It proves equal temperament is always the most accurate tuning.
It removes the need to compare one pitch to another.

items.title: Name three partials
items.body: List the 2nd, 3rd, and 5th partials as ratios above the fundamental.

items.title: Connect ratio to interval
items.body: Match one ratio from the lesson, such as 3/2 or 5/4, to the interval quality it suggests.

items.title: Compare low and high harmonics
items.body: Keep the fundamental sounding in the lab. Compare harmonics 3 and 4 with 15 and 16. Describe how their spacing changes.
